course_name_original: Diseño de máquinas hidráulicas y sistemas oleoneumáticos
course_name_en: Design of Hydraulic Machines and Oleo-Pneumatic Systems
prerequisites: To enroll in this course, it is necessary to have passed or be enrolled in all subjects from courses lower than the one in which this subject is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to calculate and design fluid machines, their installations and their operation
Ability to design pneumatic and hydraulic installations and to dimension their elements

syllabus_topics: Pneumatics and Hydraulics: Pneumatic circuits and installations
Pneumatics and Hydraulics: Electropneumatic circuits and installations
Pneumatics and Hydraulics: Hydraulic circuits and installations
Design and selection of pneumatic elements: Design of Positive Displacement Pneumatic Machines (PDPN): Compressors, Motors, and Linear Actuators
Design and selection of hydraulic elements: Design of hydraulic valves: Valves and control elements, constituting hydraulic circuits
Design and selection of hydraulic elements: Design of hydraulic elements: Design of Auxiliary Elements for Hydraulic Circuits
Introduction: 1. Introduction
Introduction: 1.1. General theory of machine design.
Introduction: 1.2. Application to the design of hydraulic machines and oleo-pneumatic systems
Design of hydraulic turbopumps: 2.1. Design and calculation of radial or centrifugal, axial, and diagonal turbopumps.
Design of hydraulic turbopumps: 2.2. Constitutive elements of turbopumps: Design, calculation, and manufacturing materials.
Design of hydraulic turbopumps: 2.3. Selection and regulation of pumps
Design of impulse and reaction turbines: 3.1. IMPULSE TURBINES 3.1.1 Design and calculation of impulse turbines. PELTON Turbines
Design of impulse and reaction turbines: 3.2. REACTION TURBINES 3.2.1. Design and calculation of axial reaction turbines. KAPLAN Turbines
Design of impulse and reaction turbines: 3.2.2. Design and calculation of radial reaction turbines. FRANCIS Turbines
Design of impulse and reaction turbines: 3.2.3. Constitutive elements of hydraulic turbines: Design, calculation, and manufacturing materials.
Compound turbomachines: 4.1. Hydraulic transmissions
Design of fans: 5.1. Introduction to fans.
Design of fans: 5.2. Design of fans.
PRACTICES: Pneumatics Practice (1-2-3) 1. Introduction to pneumatic systems: Description of pneumatic systems and their components I. Basic circuits I. Cylinder control.

PRACTICES: Electropneumatics Practice (1-2-3) 2. Description of electropneumatic systems and their components II. Basic circuits II. Use of pneumatic valves. Synthesis of logical functions with pneumatic systems. Pneumatic control.
PRACTICES: 3. Resolution of proposed problems.
PRACTICES: MDP – Pneumatic Actuators Practice.
PRACTICES: MDP – Identification of elements and machines Practice.
PRACTICES: MDP – Piston Pump Practice.
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices: Concepts developed in each topic will be applied to the realization of laboratory practices. Fundamentally, experimentation activities will be carried out, although practical cases, simulation, problem-solving, and collaborative learning may also be performed.
Autonomous problem solving: Students will solve problems posed during class hours, working autonomously.

Problem-solving: Concepts developed in each topic will be applied to solving exercises. Includes activities such as: Readings, Seminars, Problem-solving, Collaborative learning, Study of practical cases.

Lecture: The fundamentals of each topic will be explained for subsequent practical problem solving. Activities such as: Lecture session, Readings, Diagrams, Conferences, Oral presentation may be carried out.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practices: Experimental practices and written report, evaluating technical and content quality, presentation, and analysis capacity.
Autonomous problem solving: Individual resolution of problems on Pneumatics, Electropneumatics, Hydraulics, and Turbomachinery.
Group project: Written report, implemented technical knowledge, and class presentation on Pneumatics and Hydraulics.
Written test: May include theoretical questions, practical questions, problem-solving, essay, or multiple-choice questions.
Written test: May include theoretical questions, practical questions, problem-solving, essay, or multiple-choice questions.

assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation in the first opportunity, attendance at `Resolución de problemas y/o ejercicios` tests and 80% of practical hours is mandatory, requiring a minimum of 40% in each test. If the sum of grades exceeds 5.0 but the 40% minimum per test is not met, a grade of 4.5 will be recorded. For the second opportunity in continuous evaluation, students can retake tests over 30% that were not passed, retaining grades for tests scored 50% or higher; a 40% minimum per test is still required, with a 4.5 recorded if the sum is above 5.0 but individual minimums are missed. For global evaluation, a single exam covering 100% of the grade will be administered, including theoretical questions, practical problems, and experimental practices. Unethical behavior, such as copying or plagiarism, will result in a failing grade of 0.0 for the academic year.
